text:
janelle (support): FYI customer reported a sharp p95/p99 regression on streaming responses starting ~2026-03-12. They say TTFB went from ~120ms to ~800–900ms for many requests. Non-streaming (sync) endpoints appear OK. Ticket #12345.

janelle (support): repro steps they gave: curl to /v1/streams with small prompt, node fetch streaming example, headers: Authorization, model: redwood-llama-13b, stream: true. They included request id and some sample traces.

janelle (support): customer included snippet (pasted):
```
# streaming curl they used
curl -v -N \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-13b","prompt":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

janelle (support): their timeline: before 2026-03-12 p95 ~120ms TTFB; after p95 jumped to ~800ms, p99 >1.2s. They said chunks arrive normally once first chunk shows. So total completion is similar for long responses, but first-byte latency spikes.

diego (eng-runtime): thanks — can you paste the exact request-id(s) from their logs? need to correlate with service logs and runtime traces. also did they see any 5xx?

janelle (support): request ids: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c3e, r-0a1b2c3f. no 5xx, responses eventually stream fine. attached user's small server-side trace showing:
```
[2026-03-12T09:14:22Z] request r-0a1b2c3d queued -> assigned runtime node-23
[2026-03-12T09:14:22Z] runtime: accept request, model=redwood-llama-13b, seq_len=40
[2026-03-12T09:14:23Z] runtime: kernel select ok
[2026-03-12T09:14:23Z] runtime: waiting for chunk_flush (timer=600ms)
[2026-03-12T09:14:23.6Z] runtime: flush_timer fired, sending first chunk
```

janelle (support): they highlighted the "waiting for chunk_flush (timer=600ms)" line — they think flush timer used to be 50–100ms.

sam (eng-sre): interesting. any recent changes to coalescing/flush heuristics? pinging deploy bot for recent releases.

deploy-bot: deploy event: release/v1.38.2 rolled to canary at 2026-03-11T22:03:01Z. changes: "auto-chunk-coalesce default enabled, flush_timer default 600ms".

diego (eng-runtime): that lines up. v1.38.2 enabled auto chunk coalescing to reduce token overhead and improve throughput. apparently default flush_timer moved to 600ms. that would explain higher TTFB but usually better throughput.

anya (devex): can we reproduce locally? I can run small repro against staging with and without the flag. which header can flip it off?

diego (eng-runtime): header is X-Chunk-Coalesce: off|on. default omitted -> on in v1.38.2. also runtime config: flush_ms=600 now. to reproduce, set X-Chunk-Coalesce: off and compare TTFB.

janelle (support): customer agreed to try a workaround and asked for a stable short-term fix. they rely on low TTFB for inference latency-sensitive UX.

anya (devex): quick repro commands:
```
# with coalescing (default)
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-13b","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate | ts

# disable coalescing (workaround)
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "X-Chunk-Coalesce: off" -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-13b","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate | ts
```

anya (devex): on staging I see median TTFB ~110ms with coalesce=off, but ~650ms when on. p95 similar to what customer reported.

sam (eng-sre): confirmed. staging pods running runtime v1.38.2 show flush_timer=600ms. older runtime v1.37.7 had flush_timer=80ms.

diego (eng-runtime): root cause confirmed: v1.38.2 changed default chunking strategy. trade-off was throughput/cost, but it hurts TTFB-sensitive integrations.

kevin (product): we need a triage plan: short term mitigation for affected customers, medium term opt-in/opt-out controls, and long term note in release docs.

diego (eng-runtime): mitigation options:
- immediate: enable "X-Chunk-Coalesce: off" by default for hosted API requests that opt into low-latency via new header or model param; or let support flip per-customer routing to runtime config with flush_ms=80.
- short-term: roll back default in runtime to previous flush_ms=100 while we evaluate throughput impact.
- long-term: expose streaming latency profile and allow per-key preferences in Console (low-latency vs cost-optimized).

janelle (support): customer prefers a quick workaround. ok if we route their traffic to runtime with coalesce disabled? they gave permission to try.

sam (eng-sre): I can add a routing rule for their API key to set runtime flag flush_ms=80 for the next 72 hours. will monitor p95/p99 and resource usage.

deploy-bot: action: routing rule created for api-key ak-abc-123 -> runtime-flags {"flush_ms":80, "chunk_coalesce":"off"} by sam at 2026-03-12T14:22:10Z.

diego (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a patch to make the default configurable per-deployment and add a flag to the API to request low-latency streaming. also will add metric: streaming_ttfb_ms by api_key.

anya (devex): I'll update docs and add a troubleshooting note for streaming TTFB regressions (how to flip X-Chunk-Coalesce and quick repro).

kevin (product): put this on the next postmortem/notes and we should announce in release notes that v1.38.2 changes cost/latency tradeoffs.

janelle (support): telling customer we've applied temporary routing change and asking them to verify. requesting confirmation they see p95 back to ~120ms.

janelle (support): customer reply: "we see first chunk at ~130ms now. thanks!" :thumbsup:

diego (eng-runtime): great. follow-ups: (1) patch to make default flush_ms revertable and add api flag (ticket INF-4587), (2) add metric for ttfb by key (INF-4588), (3) docs + customer comms (DOCS-221). I'll own INF-4587.

sam (eng-sre): I'll monitor for any resource spike from routing exceptions, keep the rule for 72h then evaluate.

anya (devex): will publish the staging repro snippet into internal playbook.

kevin (product): also consider telemetry to surface customers who likely prefer low-latency (chat, UI use) so we can default appropriately.

janelle (support): closing loop on ticket — customer satisfied for now. will escalate to account team if they want Dedicated.

diego (eng-runtime): marking as resolved here; will file follow-up tickets. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:"
